assessment.nobel_worthiness: Theory showed that twisted bilayer graphene has a continuum-model flat band at a magic angle, and experiment then found correlated insulators and superconductivity in it. This created the moire field. It is a clean, minimal model that explains a strongly correlated, tunable platform, and the discovery opened a very large body of work across condensed matter. Originality and impact are very high.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the decisive theoretical prediction (2011). Jarillo-Herrero's group made the 2018 experimental discovery, with Cao as first author, a junior researcher not on the credited list. A two-sided theory plus experiment prize is coherent. Credit for the moire platform could also extend to other groups, for example for related moire-superlattice work, and I cannot verify how that would be allocated.
assessment.maturity: Experimental results have been reproduced by many independent groups and the flat-band picture is robust. The origin of the superconductivity and the competing phases are still debated, so the application of the theory is not fully settled. Recognition is timely but could be considered slightly early.
uncertainties: The mechanism of superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene is unresolved.
Whether the Nobel scope should include the experimental first author or other moire pioneers is unclear to me.
Sample-to-sample variability and twist-angle disorder complicate interpretation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Fluctuation theorems and the Jarzynski equality give exact, universal relations for systems far from equilibrium, generalising the second law and linking work distributions to free energies. This is the kind of simple, general mechanism I value in statistical physics. It has been verified experimentally in single-molecule and mesoscopic systems and underlies stochastic thermodynamics.
assessment.attribution: The credited trio is the classic core: Evans, Cohen and Searles (and Evans-Morriss) on the transient and steady-state fluctuation relations, Gallavotti and Cohen on the chaotic hypothesis, and Jarzynski on the work equality. Crooks, Cohen, Searles and Kurchan are also important and are not in the credited list, so a three-person prize leaves out contributors. Allocation is genuinely contested.
assessment.maturity: Experimental tests (optical tweezers on RNA unfolding, colloids, electronic and quantum devices) are many and independent. The theory is mathematically stable, and recognition would be mature, since it has been decades since the central results.
uncertainties: Several equally important contributors (Crooks, Cohen, Searles, Kurchan) are missing from the credited names.
The physical weight compared with other prize topics is arguable because it is largely conceptual.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Vicsek's minimal flocking model and the Toner-Tu hydrodynamic theory established that collective motion of self-propelled units forms a new nonequilibrium phase, with long-range order in two dimensions that violates Mermin-Wagner and with giant number fluctuations. The theory is universal, analytically tractable and exemplifies how a simple mechanism explains messy biological and synthetic systems. Importance and originality are high.
assessment.attribution: Vicsek et al. (1995) provided the numerical model, Toner and Tu (1995, 1998) the renormalisation-group hydrodynamics, and Ramaswamy with collaborators the active-gel and orientation-fluctuation theory. The attribution is plausible, though Simha, Marchetti, Lubensky and others also have large claims.
assessment.maturity: Experimental confirmation is broad but sometimes indirect (bacteria, vibrated granular rods, Janus colloids, and flocks), and the nature of the Vicsek transition (first versus second order) has been debated. The area is still evolving, which argues for slightly later recognition.
uncertainties: Quantitative experimental tests of the Toner-Tu exponents are limited.
Other major contributors may have equal claims, which could complicate a three-person split.
Natural-system relevance is partly qualitative.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamical mean-field theory becomes exact in infinite dimensions and maps lattice models onto a self-consistent quantum impurity problem. It gave the first controlled description of the Mott transition and, combined with ab initio methods, became a standard tool for correlated materials. It is a clean, general framework that is well understood.
assessment.attribution: Metzner and Vollhardt (1989) identified the infinite-dimension limit, Georges and Kotliar (1992) made the impurity mapping, and Muller-Hartmann also contributed in that period. Georges, Kotliar and Vollhardt are a defensible trio, though Metzner and Muller-Hartmann are real omissions in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: The method is mature and has been used and benchmarked for three decades. It is not a measurement-based discovery, and some voices consider it a technique rather than a discovery, which may lower its standing with an experiment-weighted committee.
uncertainties: It is a computational method, so the discovery-versus-tool question matters.
Metzner and Muller-Hartmann are not credited.
Limits for real materials (non-local correlations) are known.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological order and long-range entanglement provide a new classification of quantum phases beyond Landau symmetry breaking, with anyonic excitations and robust degeneracy. This idea is deeply original and conceptually unifying, and it links condensed matter, quantum information and spin liquids.
assessment.attribution: Wen introduced topological order and its invariants; Kitaev contributed the toric code, anyon models and the classification. A two-person prize is clean. Credit overlaps with Read, Levin, Kitaev-Preskill and others on the entanglement-based characterisation, which is not on this list.
assessment.maturity: Direct experimental confirmation of topological order in a real material is limited (spin-liquid candidates remain ambiguous), though quantum simulators now realise toric-code states. The concept is mature in theory but less so in experimental verification.
uncertainties: Experimental evidence in solids is incomplete.
Overlap with the quantum-error-correction candidate and with anyon work could cause allocation problems.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum error correction showed that fragile quantum information can be protected, which made fault-tolerant quantum computing possible in principle. This is foundational and now realised experimentally. Its conceptual depth, combining information theory and physics, is high.
assessment.attribution: Shor and Steane independently found the first quantum codes in 1995 and 1996, and Kitaev supplied topological codes and fault tolerance. Calderbank and Gottesman (stabilizer formalism), Knill, Laflamme and Aharonov, Ben-Or are important and not credited, so the trio is open to dispute.
assessment.maturity: Recent below-threshold surface-code demonstrations and logical qubits in trapped ions and Rydberg arrays give strong independent confirmation, and the timing is good, though a full fault-tolerant machine is still far away.
uncertainties: The physics-versus-computer-science balance is uncertain.
Several key contributors beyond the three credited are excluded.
Practical fault tolerance is not yet demonstrated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Biomolecular condensates showed that liquid-liquid phase separation organises cell interiors (P granules, nucleoli), which brought soft-matter and statistical physics into cell biology. It is a good example of cross-disciplinary physics with a simple underlying mechanism.
assessment.attribution: Brangwynne, Hyman and Jülicher produced the 2009 P-granule liquid-droplet work and its theoretical interpretation. The idea has many contributors (Rosen, Parker, Pappu, Mittag and Fawzi, and earlier colloid and polymer physics), so the credit is spread, and the field is arguably biology or chemistry in prize terms.
assessment.maturity: The field is large and active but contains many disputes about physiological relevance, specificity, and whether the 'liquid' description is always valid. This suggests the interpretation is not yet stable.
uncertainties: Whether this falls into the physics prize scope is uncertain.
Physiological significance is contested.
Wide credit dispersion.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The geometric phase (Berry 1984, with Aharonov-Anandan generalisation) is a universal mechanism that appears in molecules, optics, condensed matter and topological band theory, and it underlies Chern numbers and the Hall conductance. It is simple, general and very widely used.
assessment.attribution: Berry is the clear originator, Aharonov and Anandan extended it, and Pancharatnam (1956), Simon and Wilczek-Zee also have strong precursor or complementary claims. Aharonov's key work (Aharonov-Bohm effect, Aharonov-Anandan) leaves Bohm out and may be treated as separate, so the pairing is imperfect.
assessment.maturity: Experimental confirmations across optics, NMR and neutron interferometry are extensive and mature. Recognition would be late rather than premature.
uncertainties: The priority of Pancharatnam and others complicates the credit.
Berry-phase prize relevance may have been partly covered by prior topological-matter prizes (2016).
